The '''1984–85 Bundesliga''' was the 22nd season of the [[Bundesliga]], the premier football league in [[West Germany]]. It began on 24 August 1984<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=326293|title=Schedule Round 1|publisher=DFB}}</ref> and ended on 8 June 1985.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=326655|title=Archive 1984/1985 Round 34|publisher=DFB}}</ref> [[VfB Stuttgart]] were the defending champions.

==Competition modus==
Every team played two games against each other team, one at home and one away. Teams received two points for a win and one point for a draw. If two or more teams were tied on points, places were determined by [[goal difference]] and, if still tied, by goals scored. The team with the most points were crowned champions while the two teams with the fewest points were relegated to [[2. Bundesliga]]. The third-to-last team had to compete in a two-legged relegation/promotion play-off against the third-placed team from 2. Bundesliga.

==Team changes to 1983–84==
[[Kickers Offenbach]] and [[1. FC Nürnberg]] were directly relegated to the [[1984–85 2. Bundesliga|2. Bundesliga]] after finishing in the last two places. They were replaced by [[Karlsruher SC]] and [[FC Schalke 04]]. Relegation/promotion play-off participant [[Eintracht Frankfurt]] won on aggregate against [[MSV Duisburg]] and thus retained their Bundesliga status.

==Relegation play-offs==
[[Arminia Bielefeld]] and third-placed [[1984–85 2. Bundesliga|2. Bundesliga]] team [[1. FC Saarbrücken]] had to compete in a two-legged relegation/promotion play-off. Saarbrücken won 3–1 on aggregate and thus were promoted to the Bundesliga.
